definitions.explanation: The number three when counting things using native Japanese numbers.

examples.japanese: りんごを{三|みっ}つください。
{質問|しつもん}が{三|みっ}つあります。
{大|おお}きな{荷物|にもつ}が{三|みっ}つ{届|とど}いた。
{三|みっ}つの{方法|ほうほう}があるから、{好|す}きなのを{選|えら}んでください。
examples.english: There are three methods, so please choose the one you like.

notes:
{三|みっ}つ is the native Japanese number for counting three general items.

NATIVE COUNTING SYSTEM (1-10):
- {一|ひと}つ (1), {二|ふた}つ (2), {三|みっ}つ (3), {四|よっ}つ (4), {五|いつ}つ (5)
- {六|むっ}つ (6), {七|なな}つ (7), {八|やっ}つ (8), {九|ここの}つ (9), {十|とお} (10)

WHEN TO USE:
- General objects without specific counters
- Age up to 9: {三|みっ}つ = 3 years old
- Abstract things: {理由|りゆう}が{三|みっ}つ (three reasons)

CHINESE VS. NATIVE:
- {三|さん}: Sino-Japanese (used with counters)
- {三|みっ}つ: Native Japanese (standalone counting)

EXAMPLE CONTRAST:
- りんごを{三|みっ}つ: three apples (native)
- りんごを{三|さん}{個|こ}: three apples (Sino-Japanese)
